correctness.rationale: Every tree on K_{2,n} has one double-edge right vertex and independent single-edge choices elsewhere. Its minimum weight at a fixed doubled index j is the sum of all column minima plus the jth column maximum. The unique minimizing maximum index is uniform over n columns; independently, the signs selecting each minimum are independent fair coins because paired weights are iid and atomless. Hence each of exactly n 2^(n-1) trees has probability 1/(n 2^(n-1)). Conditioning on the index proves the exact strict negative covariances. No moment or density assumptions were introduced. Checker exhausts all 24, 720, 40320 orders for K2,2 through K2,4, with exact edge/pair rational assertions, and finds nonuniform K3,3. The finite checks are not extrapolated.

value.rationale: The identity characterizes the complete probability distribution for infinitely many K_{2,n} networks, which contain overlapping cycles for n>=3 and are not explained by independent edge deletion on cactus cycles. This gives an exact sharp probabilistic comparison of random MST and UST in the currently studied dependence setting, together with edge covariances of order one for within-column pairs and order n^-2 for across-column pairs. The exact K3,3 boundary check confirms the phenomenon is special, not a generic consequence of bipartiteness. This is a complete motivated structural case, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
